title: Life interval
description: What the life stage writes: for one fill or piece and one history layer, a span of years in which the layer runs at one rate from one reset. The layer's value at a date is its material's curve at rate / 1000 x (date - resetYear + ageOffsetMonths / 12) (decisions D5.1). The texel inputs in the place and history pages are baked from these. All integers: years and months, per mille.

on.description: The fill or piece it is about. A replaced part is a new fill and so starts its own intervals.

to.description: Null while it still runs at the fabric date.

resetYear.description: The year the layer last started from nothing: the stone laid, the face bared, the coat put on.

rate.description: Per mille of the material's own rate: 1000 runs the curve as the material record gives it.

ageOffsetMonths.description: Age the surface brought with it, in months: a reclaimed stone's years in the heap, or a negative offset where a layer starts late.

cause.description: The event or rule that started this interval (a works campaign, falling care, a gutter that failed).
